title: Ethiopian History University Entrance Exam 2018
description: Ethiopian History University Entrance Exam 2018 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: How did the early Industrial Revolution create social inequity in the share of national wealth?
options: By raising living standards with the national growth
By giving privileges for factory owners who exploited workers
By providing quality items with lower prices for the people
By maintaining trade balance between Europe and Africa
questions.explanation: During the early Industrial Revolution, immense wealth was accumulated by factory owners and capitalists who profited heavily while exploiting low-wage, overworked laborers, thereby widening social inequity.

questions.questionText: What was the major factor for 'the Eastern Question' in the Balkan region?
options: The interest of Russia to protect the sovereignty of Austria
The ambition of Austria-Hungary to expand its territories
The growth of the British colonial interest in the region
The declining power of Ottoman Turkey in the region
questions.explanation: The 'Eastern Question' centered primarily around the geopolitical crisis and power vacuum created by the progressive decline and fragmentation of the Ottoman Empire (Ottoman Turkey).

questions.questionText: What difficulty did the European powers face to penetrate deep into the African interior in the early stage?
options: Strong clan resistance
Financial constraint
Lack of modern arms
Mosquito and Tsetse fly
questions.explanation: Tropical diseases transmitted by mosquitoes (such as malaria) and tsetse flies posed lethal barriers to Europeans and their livestock, heavily delaying deep interior exploration until quinine and other preventatives became available.

questions.questionText: What was the response of the British colonial governors in Serra Leon to the demands of Samori Ture who was fighting against French colonialism?
options: To Mandinka under the British protection
To sell modern weapons for him
To be involved directly in the war
To send their military force to Mandinka
questions.explanation: British colonial authorities in Sierra Leone engaged with Samori Ture by trading modern firearms and weapons with him, viewing him as a buffer against French colonial expansion.

questions.questionText: How did the British government aim to implement indirect rule in Africa?
options: By integrating the Africans into the British custom
By employing new local chiefs loyal to the colonial masters
By representing Africans elects in the British parliament
By separating the African pre-colonial chiefdom administration
questions.explanation: Indirect rule relied on utilizing existing traditional authorities or appointing compliant local chiefs who were loyal to the British colonial administration to govern and collect taxes on their behalf.

questions.questionText: What were the two destinations of the long-distance trade that passed through the city of Gondar in the 19th century?
options: Tajura and Obock
Adwa and Port Sudan
Metemma and Massawa
Sudan and Egypt
questions.explanation: In the 19th century, Gondar served as a major commercial hub connected to northern and northwestern trade routes leading towards Metemma (toward Sudan) and Massawa (toward the Red Sea coast).

questions.questionText: What was the main factor for the failure of Tewodros's modernization efforts?
options: The regional and foreign challenge encountered him.
Britain refused to give support for his modernization plan.
The Egyptian aggression obstructed to implement his plan.
He suffered from shortage of time to modify his plan.
questions.explanation: Emperor Tewodros II faced continuous internal regional rebellions and severe foreign challenges (including diplomatic isolation and British opposition), which severely undermined and distracted from his centralization and modernization efforts.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct regarding the situation of the Arsi Oromo after the battle of Azule?
options: They paid less tribute than those submitted peacefully.
They were allowed to re-install their local institutions.
Their rulers began to be assigned from the center.
Their local autonomy was preserved as in the past.
questions.explanation: Following their defeat at the Battle of Azule and subsequent subjugation, the traditional governance of the Arsi Oromo was dismantled, and administrators/rulers began to be appointed directly from the central government.

questions.questionText: Why did Emperor Yohannis IV spend most of his time in the battle fields? Because he determined to
options: punish those who disrupted peace.
show his huge military power.
crush mainly local rebellions.
fight against foreign aggressions.
questions.explanation: Emperor Yohannes IV spent a large portion of his reign defending the country's sovereignty on multiple fronts against foreign aggressions and incursions, including Egyptians, Mahdists, and Italians.

questions.questionText: What was the immediate reaction of Ethiopia to the Italian aggression of 1935?
options: Appealed to the League of Nations.
Declared outright conventional war.
Opted diplomatic discussion with Italy.
Resisted them through guerilla warfare.
questions.explanation: Following the 1935 Italian invasion, Emperor Haile Selassie's government immediately appealed to the League of Nations for collective security and diplomatic intervention against the aggression.

questions.questionText: Which of the following defines the discipline of history? It studies about
options: myth of a given society.
current political developments.
human experience in the past.
recent societal interactions.
questions.explanation: History is academically defined as the systematic study and interpretation of past human experiences, activities, and societies.

questions.questionText: In which century did the Hejira take place? In the
options: 8th century A. D.
7th century A. D.
7th century B.C.
8th century B.C.
questions.explanation: The Hejira (Hijra), Prophet Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina, occurred in 622 A.D., which places it in the 7th century A.D.

questions.questionText: How did the Neolithic Revolution change the life of human beings?
options: By making them food producers
By introducing market centers
By producing refined stone tools
By making them to be hunter-gatherer
questions.explanation: The Neolithic Revolution marked the monumental transition from nomadic hunting and gathering to sedentary agriculture and domestication, making humans food producers.

questions.questionText: Which language super-family is widely spoken in Ethiopia?
options: Khoisan
Nilo-Sahara
Afro-Asiatic
Niger-Congo
questions.explanation: Afro-Asiatic is the dominant language super-family in Ethiopia, encompassing major language families such as Cushitic, Semitic, and Omotic.

questions.questionText: What was a common element to the American civilizations up to the 16th century?
options: They had one administrative center.
They were established by the Spaniards.
They were agrarian states emerged along river valleys.
They were destroyed by Spanish colonizers.
questions.explanation: Major pre-Columbian American civilizations (such as the Aztecs and Incas) ultimately faced collapse and destruction following the arrival of Spanish conquistadors and colonizers in the 16th century.

questions.questionText: In what way did the ancient Greece civilization influence the modern world?
options: By advancing the ancient Roman civilization
By introducing the Western philosophy
By introducing the concept of state formation
By making successful military conquest
questions.explanation: Ancient Greece made foundational contributions to Western thought, laying the basis for modern philosophy, democratic concepts, science, and literature.

questions.questionText: Why did the Roman government begin to persecuting Christians in the 1st century? Because they considered them as a
options: monotheistic believers.
reformist in their empire.
followers of Jewish religion.
threat to the empire unity.
questions.explanation: Early Christians refused to participate in the imperial cult and worship the Roman emperor, which the Roman authorities viewed as a threat to state loyalty and empire unity.

questions.questionText: What was the base for the economic prosperity of the Aksumite state?
options: Gold mining
Renting Ships
Internal and external trade
Nomadic pastoralism
questions.explanation: The Aksumite state's economic prosperity was primarily built upon its flourishing internal and extensive international trade network connecting the Red Sea, the Mediterranean, and the Indian Ocean.

questions.questionText: What was the main factor for the decline of the Zagwe kingdom?
options: The problem of succession among the Zagwe rulers.
It lost the support of the Orthodox clergy.
The control of the Red Sea by the Muslim Arabs.
It failed to secure the trade routes that linked to the Zeila.
questions.explanation: Internal conflicts, political instability, and recurring problems of peaceful succession among the Zagwe rulers significantly weakened the kingdom.

questions.questionText: What was the common feature of the Christian Kingdom before and after Yekuno Amlak?
options: Continued to have the same territorial stretch.
Constructed several Rock-hewn churches.
Attempted to homogenize the people under its rule.
Maintained the prevailing Christian culture.
questions.explanation: Throughout the transitions in ruling dynasties, the Christian Kingdom consistently preserved, promoted, and maintained the prevailing Ethiopian Orthodox Christian culture and tradition.

questions.questionText: Which of the following accelerated the birth of early capitalist relations?
options: Growth of new industrial compound unit
Guarantee of Legal equality of all citizens
Involvement of the feudal class in investment
Towns that facilitated developments of trade
questions.explanation: The revival and growth of medieval towns and urban centers acted as major catalysts for commerce, markets, and the development of early capitalist economic relations.

questions.questionText: Why did the ideas of the period of the Renaissance has lasting impacts?
options: It promoted the church's view about space.
It gave emphasis to humanity tied with dignity.
It upheld understanding of the world through faith.
It appreciated surviving states on the bases of law.
questions.explanation: The Renaissance had a profound and lasting impact by championing humanism, which placed strong emphasis on human potential, reason, and individual dignity.

questions.questionText: Which of the following feature is correct regarding the Almohad movement?
options: It declared Quran as the only source of Islam.
It valued aristocratic norm that exposed woman.
It liked the use of musical instruments.
It was a factor for the decline of Ghana.
questions.explanation: The Almohad movement and its expansion in North Africa and West Africa significantly impacted and contributed to the decline of the Ghana Empire.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factor enabled ancient Ghana to build large Empire?
options: Availability of a warrior population
The support it enjoyed from the Almohad
The importation of arms from Europe
Development of iron working technology
questions.explanation: The mastery and development of iron working technology allowed ancient Ghana to forge superior weapons and agricultural tools, boosting its military power and economic foundation.

questions.questionText: What factor helped the Swahili states of the East African coast to reach their zenith from the 11th to the 15th centuries?
options: The thriving trade across the Indian Ocean
Contact with China during the reign of Zheng He
The custom posts of the various trading towns
The coming of the Portuguese to the coast
questions.explanation: The Swahili city-states prospered and reached their peak between the 11th and 15th centuries primarily through thriving maritime commerce and trade across the Indian Ocean.

questions.questionText: What was the reason contributed for the greatness of Zimbabwe in the 14th century?
options: Meat trade with the Dutch settlers in South Africa
Commercial links in gold with the neighboring coastal cities
Conquest of neighboring states to grab large resources
Development of regional cottage industry at household level
questions.explanation: Great Zimbabwe's wealth and power in the 14th century were built on its control over gold mining and lucrative commercial links connecting the interior with coastal trading ports.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was the achievement of the pre-colonial state of Dahomey?
options: Construction of remarkable stone walls
Intensification of surplus production
Introduction of modern government system
Formation of qualified women regiments
questions.explanation: The West African kingdom of Dahomey was famously known for its military organization, notably including elite and highly trained female military regiments (often called the Dahomey Amazons).

questions.questionText: How did the advance of the "Trek Boers" highly endanger the survival of the native Khoi-Khoi people in South Africa?
options: The conflict with the Boers led the British involvement in the war.
The Boer's military camp forced the Khoisan to leave their home land.
The extensive white settlement was accompanied with deadly diseases.
The raiding of cattle by the Boers threatened Khoi-Khoi livelihood.
questions.explanation: The advance of the Trek Boers directly threatened the traditional pastoral livelihood of the Khoi-Khoi through extensive cattle raiding, land dispossession, and destruction of their herds.

questions.questionText: In which part of Africa were the missionaries successful in achieving their objectives?
options: Central Africa
Western Africa
Northern Africa
Eastern Africa
questions.explanation: Christian missionary activities and evangelization found significant and enduring success in Sub-Saharan regions, particularly in Eastern and Southern Africa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factor has enabled the restoration of the 'Solomonic' dynasty possible?
options: Strong military operation conducted by Yekuno Amlak.
Anti Aksumite propaganda by the Orthodox church.
The legend of the Queen of Sheba empowered Yekuno Amlak.
Unity of Yekuno Amlak with rebels that opposed Yitbarek.
questions.explanation: Yekuno Amlak successfully rallied various regional opposition groups and rebel forces who opposed the last Zagwe ruler, Yitbarek, enabling the overthrow and the establishment of the 'Solomonic' dynasty.

questions.questionText: How did the unification of Italy realize?
options: Through popular revolution
By widening political difference among states
Through integrating diplomacy and wars
Peacefully by effort of the Catholic Church
questions.explanation: The unification of Italy was achieved through a strategic combination of astute diplomacy (such as Cavour's alliances) and military campaigns and wars (including nationalist uprisings and French/Austrian conflicts).

questions.questionText: What enabled Prussia to play a leading role in the unification of Germany?
options: It emerged as the dominant European state during the 1848 revolutions.
It gained the legitimacy of leadership from other states.
It dominated the German Confederation formed in 1815.
It possessed a capable army confronting challenges.
questions.explanation: Prussia possessed a highly disciplined, modernized, and powerful military apparatus under Bismarck's leadership, which successfully waged wars to defeat external rivals and unify Germany.

questions.questionText: Why did Europeans achieve victory over Africans during the colonial conquest?
options: Europeans were possessed with modern arms.
Europeans won the support of many Africans.
Africans sought Europe as civilization agents.
African leaders not resistance against colonist.
questions.explanation: The decisive technological gap, particularly European possession of advanced modern weaponry (like repeating rifles and machine guns), was a primary factor in their military victories during the scramble for Africa.

questions.questionText: What propaganda did the Maji Maji leaders use that would turn German bullets harmless?
options: Sprinkling the body with sacred water
Calling the name of gods on the enemy
Spreading in a wide area during attack
Praying on the eve of major battle
questions.explanation: During the Maji Maji Rebellion in German East Africa, leaders used sacred water (mixed with maize grains and sorghum) called 'Maji', promising that it would turn German bullets into harmless water.

questions.questionText: Which one is correct regarding the role of long-distance trade in Ethiopia?
options: It led to intensive competition among merchants.
It promoted misunderstanding among different people.
It encouraged interaction among different people.
It confined merchants in their respective area.
questions.explanation: Long-distance trade routes served as vital economic and cultural bridges that linked diverse regions, thus encouraging social interaction, exchange, and integration among different peoples and cultures.

questions.questionText: What was the effect of the Qalad system introduced by the imperial system during the reign of Menelik II?
options: It facilitated taxes collection system.
It led to wide spread rebellion in the country.
It enlarged the land owned by the church.
It facilitated land redistribution for the landless.
questions.explanation: The Qalad system was a measurement and land assessment system introduced to organize and streamline measurement for taxation and tribute collection.

questions.questionText: What was the major feature of the Diarchy rule in Ethiopia?
options: The collaboration of the progressives with the conservatists
The growing power of Ras Teferi over Empress Zawditu
The revitalization of the power of the various regional lords
The exposure of Ethiopia to European colonial ambition
questions.explanation: The period of the diarchy (dual rule) between Empress Zawditu and Ras Teferi Makonnen was characterized by the progressive rise and consolidation of power by Ras Teferi relative to the Empress.

questions.questionText: Why was the League of Nations criticized largely as a weak organization? Because it
options: lacked regulation for admission and removal of membership.
reinforced decisions by the majority vote of its members.
used strong armed intervention to stop territorial disputes.
failed to prevent the outbreak of another world war.
questions.explanation: The League of Nations was widely deemed a failure and criticized as weak primarily because it lacked the enforcement mechanisms and authority to stop aggressive expansions, ultimately failing to prevent the outbreak of World War II.

questions.questionText: How did the German army overrun France during the Second World War? By advancing through
options: neutral Holland and Belgium.
Italy and satellite territories.
the well defended western border.
the French border directly.
questions.explanation: During World War II, the German army bypassed the heavily fortified Maginot Line by invading and advancing through neutral Belgium and the Netherlands (similar to the Schlieffen Plan strategy) to quickly defeat France.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes feature of the Cold War? It was a period of
options: an active armed conflict in Europe.
tactical trench warfare with mercenaries.
proxy-war mostly in Asia and Africa.
war that lacked military camps.
questions.explanation: The Cold War was characterized by ideological conflict and proxy wars fought primarily in developing regions across Asia and Africa, avoiding direct major military engagement between the superpowers.

questions.questionText: Which of the following events was directly related to the immediate outbreak of the WWI?
options: The German invasion against neutral Belgium
The Russian support for Serbia against Austro-Hungary
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
The British declaration of war against Germany
questions.explanation: The immediate spark that triggered the outbreak of World War I was the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914.

questions.questionText: Why did the consequence of the Russian Revolution become a global concern? Because it
options: was the first popular revolution that changed government.
designed the dominant ideology in the Western Europe.
created an ideology contrary to the capitalist system.
was the first revolution that led to democratization.
questions.explanation: The Russian Revolution established the world's first socialist state based on Marxism-Leninism, creating an economic and political ideology fundamentally contrary to the global capitalist system.

questions.questionText: Why did the capitalist economy of the interwar period suffer from depression?
options: The collapse of old regimes caused the reign of instability.
Restrictive trade practice led to the collapse of global commerce.
Due to self-sufficiency of all nations the trade setting was disturbed.
The rise of militaristic government ruined stock markets.
questions.explanation: During the interwar period, protectionist and restrictive trade practices (such as high tariffs) severely choked international trade, contributing deeply to the collapse of global commerce and the Great Depression.

questions.questionText: Which Organ of the United Nation is responsible to assign an ad-hoc committees for a special mission?
options: General Assembly
Security Council
Trusteeship Council
The Secretariat
questions.explanation: The United Nations General Assembly is empowered to establish various ad-hoc committees, subsidiary organs, and special missions to deal with specific tasks and issues.

questions.questionText: What was the fundamental cause of the Cold War?
options: Proxy-war
Berlin Blockade
Marshall Plan
Superpower rivalry
questions.explanation: The fundamental cause of the Cold War was the deep geopolitical, economic, and ideological superpower rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union.

questions.questionText: What major economic reform did the CCP government of China take to alleviate the miserable life of peasants?
options: Redistributed land to the landless.
Paid reparation for peasants.
Issued the maternity law.
Modified the rate of various taxes.
questions.explanation: Following the Chinese Communist Party's victory, major agrarian reforms were implemented which redistributed land from landlords to landless peasants.

questions.questionText: Why did Ethiopia basically argue to reclaim over Eritrea?
options: To challenge the neo-colonialist British domination in Est Africa
To secure its allegiance of access to the sea and national defense
To deconstruct suggestions of the Four Powers Commission
To safeguard the supporters of Unionism in Eritrea
questions.explanation: Ethiopia's primary argument for federation/reclamation with Eritrea centered on securing vital sovereign access to the sea for trade and ensuring national defense.

questions.questionText: What was the quest of Ethiopian students' movement in its first phase?
options: Improvements in learning facilities
Closure of the Parliament
Resignation of the Monarchy
Redistribution of land for peasant
questions.explanation: The famous slogan and core quest of the early phase of the Ethiopian student movement was 'Land to the Tiller', focusing on rural land reform and peasant rights.

questions.questionText: What was the demand of the civilian population after Derg seized power?
options: Severe punishment on the officials of the old regime
Establishment of all-inclusive people's government
Consolidation of the military government
Redistribution of the wealth of the feudal lords
questions.explanation: Following the downfall of the imperial regime, popular civilian movements and groups strongly demanded the establishment of a broad-based, all-inclusive democratic people's government instead of military rule.

questions.questionText: Which campaign of the Derg is considered as more successful than others?
options: The Literacy Campaign
The Green Campaign
The Red Star Campaign
The Development Campaign
questions.explanation: The National Literacy Campaign launched by the Derg in the 1970s and 1980s achieved widespread international acclaim and success in dramatically reducing illiteracy rates across Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about historiography?
options: It employs system to study the beginning of Human society.
It judges the past events from the perspective of the present.
It introduces school of thoughts for the historical writing.
It refers to technique of study of the historical writing.
questions.explanation: Historiography is defined as the study of the methodology and techniques of historical writing, as well as the analysis of how history has been written over time.

questions.questionText: What is the central view of the creationist theory?
options: It believes that life eventually grew from a single cell.
It rejects God's capability of creating life forms.
It believes that human beings are created by God.
It promotes Darwin's origin of species by natural selection.
questions.explanation: Creationist theory fundamentally posits that life and human beings were created by divine agency (God).

questions.questionText: How did the origin of early states associate with religion? It was when
options: religious men played secular roles like maintaining peace.
secular leaders helped by priest to maintain security.
religion and secularism integrated to keep security.
monarch played a role in leading ritual practice.
questions.explanation: In early states, political and religious authority were closely intertwined, often with the monarch or ruler serving as a chief religious figure leading ritual practices to legitimize their rule.

questions.questionText: What was the status of women in the ancient Egyptian social affair?
options: They were considered as slaves.
They had no right of inheritance.
They were less privileged than men.
They enjoyed high status than men.
questions.explanation: Compared to many other ancient civilizations, women in ancient Egypt enjoyed a relatively high legal, social, and economic status, possessing rights to own property, inherit, and enter legal contracts.

questions.questionText: Which of the following refers to the unique achievement of the Sumerians?
options: Invention of 360° as the concept of a circle
Preparation of medicine from different Herbs
Construction of various kinds of monuments
Adoption of the Confucianism philosophy
questions.explanation: The Sumerians made foundational contributions to mathematics and astronomy, including the division of the circle into 360 degrees.

questions.questionText: What was the basic factor for the introduction of Judaism into Ethiopia?
options: The visit of the Queen of Sheba of Ethiopia to King Solomon of Israel
The coming of Jewish priest accompanying Menelik I from Israel
The arrival of Jewish missionaries from Israel to serve Menelik I
The settlement of Jewish pilgrims in the Churches of Lalibela
questions.explanation: According to the Ethiopian traditional narrative detailed in the Kebra Nagast, Judaism was introduced through the return of Menelik I (son of King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba) accompanied by Israelite priests and nobles.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains the relationship of the Sultanate of Shewa with the neighboring states?
options: It established relations with the Sultanate of Adal.
It traced its origin to the Walasma ruling family.
It was the founder of the Shewan kingdom.
Its hegemony ended by the conquest of Ifat.
questions.explanation: The hegemony and rule of the Makhzumite Sultanate of Shewa came to an end when it was conquered and incorporated by the expanding Sultanate of Ifat.

questions.questionText: Why did the Bete-Israel people develop skills in artisanship? Because they were
options: encouraged by kings to diversify their economy.
forced to settle in unfavorable areas for cultivation.
denied the right of inheriting their fathers' land.
forbidden to become an agrarian community.
questions.explanation: Historically, the Bete-Israel developed specialized skills in pottery, masonry, and metalworking largely because they were restricted from owning land and denied the right of inheriting their fathers' agricultural land.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factor helped Muslim Arabs to establish large empire?
options: The military triumph over the Byzantine and Persian Empires
The war between the Abbasid and Umayyad dynasties
The assignment of local officials in the area they conquered
The Islamization of local people in all of the conquered regions
questions.explanation: The rapid expansion and establishment of the early large Arab-Muslim empire were propelled by major military triumphs over the weakened neighboring Byzantine and Sasanian (Persian) Empires.

questions.questionText: Which of the following achievement associated with the Song dynasty in China?
options: It introduced Neo-Confucianism.
It invented Gunpowder.
It made Beijing a walled city.
It employed talented officials.
questions.explanation: The Song dynasty period in China saw the flourishing and official introduction/consolidation of Neo-Confucianism as the orthodox state philosophy.

questions.questionText: What was the basic cause for the outbreak of the 1977-1978 Ethio-Somali war?
options: The decision of the OAU to unify Somali speakers
The USA-driven agenda of Somalia to crush the Derg regime
The Somalia government's claim over Ethiopia territories
The UN resolution that favored the unification of the Somali people
questions.explanation: The fundamental cause of the 1977-1978 war was the Somali government's irredentist claim and ambition to incorporate the Ogaden region and other Ethiopian territories into a 'Greater Somalia'.

questions.questionText: What was the significant progress that the French government made in its African colonies after WWII?
options: It aimed to liberate the economy of its colonies.
It allowed full independence without restriction.
It granted legislative power for the local assembly.
It made political reform within French association.
questions.explanation: Following World War II, through reforms such as the Loi Cadre and the Fourth Republic constitution, France granted increased political representation and legislative powers to local assemblies in its African territories.

questions.questionText: How did the Western World continue to dominate the economy of independent African states?
options: By deepening their influence into the local economic policy
By maintaining the colonial practices on the African economy
By opposing the establishment of large-scale industries in Africa
By refusing to lend money ever since they left the continent
questions.explanation: Through neo-colonial mechanisms, unequal terms of trade, and financial structures, Western powers continued to maintain traditional economic dependency and colonial-era economic patterns in independent Africa.

questions.questionText: In what ways did the Soviet government support Mozambique after they concluded the treaty of friendship and cooperation?
options: Deployed skilled manpower.
Established industrial centers.
Sent various munitions.
Funded the recovery plan.
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union provided military assistance, including weapons, arms, and various munitions, to the government of Mozambique after signing their treaty of friendship and cooperation.

questions.questionText: Why did the Organization of African Unity become a subject of criticism? Because it
options: lacked concern about the people of Africa.
was an agent of the UN to promote human rights.
took side while attempting to resolve civil wars.
used excessive military power in its interventions.
questions.explanation: The OAU faced widespread criticism for its principle of non-interference in member states' internal affairs, which often led to a perceived lack of action or concern regarding human rights abuses and the suffering of African peoples.

questions.questionText: How did the Transitional Governments of Ethiopia adjust the present-day administrative structure?
options: By approving the former geographic based regional formation
By establishing regional boundaries on the basis of geography
By accepting the former administrative structure
By forming the Ethnic based regional administrative units
questions.explanation: The Transitional Government of Ethiopia restructured the country into a federal system based on ethno-linguistic lines, forming ethnic-based regional administrative units.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following was a major challenge to the process of democratization in Ethiopia during the EPRDF period?
options: Presence of few opposition parties to run election
Existence of multi-party system and regional formation
Absence of formal and inclusive elections in the country
Loose implementations of human and democratic rights
questions.explanation: During the EPRDF period, critics and observers frequently pointed out the loose, inconsistent, or inadequate implementation and protection of constitutionally guaranteed human and democratic rights as a major challenge to true democratization.

questions.questionText: Why did Ethiopia send Peace Keeping Force to Rwanda?
options: To supervise election
To fight against terrorist groups
To respond to the UN mission
To realize the AU Mission
questions.explanation: Ethiopia contributed peacekeeping forces to Rwanda as part of the broader international response through United Nations missions (UNAMIR) to help restore order and aid humanitarian efforts.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following describes the features of indigenous knowledge?
options: It promotes individual gains.
It is unique to a given society.
It is easily replaceable.
It dictates how to control nature.
questions.explanation: A defining characteristic of indigenous knowledge systems is that they are deeply rooted in a particular culture, making them unique and specific to a given society or local community.

questions.questionText: Which of the following defines the role of heritages in social stability and order?
options: Erodes national and worldwide connections.
Promotes the deeds that most people tend to forget.
Emphasizes the heroism of one group over the other.
Makes people feel better, more confident and secure.
questions.explanation: Cultural heritages provide a sense of identity, continuity, and belonging, which fosters a shared community spirit and makes people feel more confident, secure, and psychologically grounded.

questions.questionText: What was the major event marked the final collapse of communism in USSR?
options: The establishment of many sovereign states in Eastern Europe
The detachment of many countries of the world from USSR
The reforms of Gorbachev peacefully dissolving the USSR
The space program of USA that weakened the power of USSR
questions.explanation: The final dissolution and collapse of the Soviet Union were marked by the formal independence and establishment of multiple sovereign states across Eastern Europe and the former Soviet republics.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains the post liberation Ethiopian politics until the 1952?
options: Administrative reforms with sophisticated political stresses.
Undermining of the country's sovereignty by foreign powers.
Settlement of armed struggles through traditional methods.
Revision of the 1931 Constitution to avoid maladministration.
questions.explanation: In the immediate post-liberation period up to 1952, Ethiopia faced strong external pressures and British military administration/interference in parts of the country, which undermined the country's complete sovereignty.

questions.questionText: What was the immediate cause for the outbreak of Gojjam peasant rebellion?
options: Corrupt administration
Ill-treatment of patriots
Religious discrimination
Agricultural tax increment
questions.explanation: The Gojjam peasant rebellion was primarily triggered and ignited by the introduction of a new, unpopular agricultural tax assessment and increment.

questions.questionText: Which reform of the Derg marked the end of the feudal system in Ethiopia?
options: Nationalization of rural land
Privatization companies and factories
Nationalization of banks and insurances
Confiscation of urban house by government
questions.explanation: The historic proclamation nationalizing rural land and abolishing tenancy ('Land to the Tiller') dismantled the economic foundation of the Ethiopian feudal aristocracy.

questions.questionText: Why did armed struggle begin in Eritrea in 1958? Because
options: Ethiopia took measures to realize the 1952 Federal Act.
Ethiopia integrated Eritrea by violating the federal act of 1952.
Eritrean people were largely in favor of living within Ethiopia.
Opposition political parties in Eritrea agreed to fight Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: The armed struggle in Eritrea began following the systematic dismantling of the federation and the full integration/annexation of Eritrea by the imperial government in violation of the UN 1952 Federal Act.

questions.questionText: Which of the following guaranteed the end of Apartheid that gave way to black majority rule in South Africa?
options: The armed struggle under 'Umkhonto we Sizwe'
The release of Nelson Mandela from prison
The introduction of 'one man, one vote' rule
The pressure coming from the United Nations
questions.explanation: The transition to democracy and the definitive end of Apartheid were constitutionally and politically sealed by the introduction of democratic elections based on the principle of 'one person, one vote'.

questions.questionText: What was the major function of regional economic communities (RECs) of Africa?
options: Linking African economy with former colonial powers
Facilitating economic integration among its members
Awakening Africans to produce multiple cash crops
Encouraging Africans to export more and import less goods
questions.explanation: Regional Economic Communities (RECs) across Africa are primarily designed to foster regional cooperation, trade liberalization, and deeper economic integration among member states as building blocks for continental unity.

questions.questionText: What was the problem that faced the Ethiopian third election of 2005 G.C?
options: The failure of opposition parties to forge a strong unified block
The refusal of opposition parties to accept the winning of ruling party
The ruling party's winning of the majority seats in Addis Ababa
The refusal of the government to accept the result of election
questions.explanation: The 2005 general election faced severe political crisis following post-election disputes, allegations of irregularities, and the refusal of major opposition groups to accept the official election results declared by the electoral board.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describe the feature of Indigenous knowledge?
options: Difficult to put into practice.
Lacks real aspect of the community.
Developed over a short period of time.
Oriented by local knowledge and language.
questions.explanation: Indigenous knowledge is deeply rooted in local environments, shared languages, and community practices, making it inherently localized and context-specific.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following practices is a customary conflict resolution mechanism?
options: Mada'a of Afar
Irrecha of Oromo
Gifata of Wolayita
Chambalala of Sidama
questions.explanation:
The Mada'a refers to the customary legal and conflict resolution system of the Afar people.

 (Note: Irrecha is a thanksgiving festival, and Chambalala/Gifata are New Year celebrations).

questions.questionText: What was the common element shared by Muslim sultanates in Ethiopia and the Horn of Africa?
options: They were administered under one Sultan.
They were vassals of the Christian kingdom.
Their Sultans exercised politico-religious power.
Their people practiced different religions.
questions.explanation: In many of the medieval Muslim sultanates of the region, the ruling sultans often combined both political/secular leadership and religious authority or legitimacy.

questions.questionText: Which of the following people was partly assimilated into the Mecha Oromo and partly moved to Gojjam?
options: Bizamo
Ennarya
Ganz
Wajj
questions.explanation: Historically, the Bizamo people (located south of the Abay River) were partly absorbed/assimilated by the expanding Mecha Oromo and partly displaced or moved toward Gojjam.

questions.questionText: What was the major cause for the conflict between the Sultanate of Adal and Christian Highland kingdom in Ethiopia?
options: Maintaining balance of power
Religious differences
Economic competition
Foreign intervention
questions.explanation: While religious factors played a role, the prolonged military conflict between the Christian Highland Kingdom and the Muslim Sultanate of Adal was primarily driven by trade routes, control of commerce, and economic competition.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factor caused the Somali population movement into the Eastern highlands in the 16th century?
options: Pressure that came from the Oromos
To give military support for Imam Ahmed
Fear of possible attack from Adal
Searching for pasture land and water
questions.explanation: The 16th-century Somali population movements were primarily driven by the search for new pasture land and water resources for their livestock.

questions.questionText: What was the common element shared among the Omotic states?
options: They exercised age-based egalitarian administration.
They practiced the Kati governance system.
They developed powerful councils over the kings.
They organized monarchial polities.
questions.explanation: Many of the Omotic states in the southwestern part of Ethiopia were characterized by centralized, monarchical political structures.

questions.questionText: What was the major factor for the transformation of the Oromo of Gibe region from Gadaa system into monarchies?
options: The growth of sedentary farming community in the region
The failure of the Gadaa institution as compatible system
The revival of the long-distance trade in the region
The adoption of the Arab's form of clan administration
questions.explanation: The transition of the Gibe Oromo societies from the traditional egalitarian Gadaa system to monarchical rule (the Gibe kingdoms) was largely fueled by economic changes, trade participation, and the growth of long-distance trade.

questions.questionText: How did the Shewan kingdom gain acceptance among the neighboring peoples in the process of consolidating its power?
options: By becoming co-religionist with them
By making marriage alliance with them
By recruiting more troops from them
By sharing the power with them
questions.explanation: The Kingdom of Shewa strategically used marriage alliances with regional leaders and neighboring groups to secure loyalty, expand influence, and consolidate power.

questions.questionText: What was the main objective of the 19th century European missionaries and explorers in Ethiopia?
options: Conducting scientific studies in many fields
Transferring European civilization to Ethiopia
Preparing the ground for later colonization
Helping Ethiopia to gain artisans from Europe
questions.explanation: Historically, European explorers and missionaries of the 19th century often acted as precursors or scouts, gathering geographical, political, and strategic intelligence that prepared the ground for subsequent colonial expansion and influence.

questions.questionText: What was the major cause for the American War of Independence?
options: The imposition of heavy taxes on the colonies by the British
The declaration of independence by the colonies
The colonial parliament refused to approve tax reduction
The Anglo-French colonial rivalry over the American land
questions.explanation: The American War of Independence was primarily triggered by the British Crown imposing heavy, unrepresented taxes and economic restrictions on the thirteen colonies.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a reform introduced by Napoleon Bonaparte?
options: Confiscation of church lands for redistribution
Guarantee of equality between women and men
Clear and complete codification of French law
Discouraged talented generals and officials
questions.explanation: One of Napoleon's most enduring achievements and reforms was the creation of the Napoleonic Code, which brought clear, rational, and complete codification to French civil law.

questions.questionText: Which of the following feature describes the state of Damot in the late 13th century?
options: It overrun the kingdom of Bizamo.
Its ruling family embraced Christianity.
It had insignificant relation with Walayita.
It brought central Ethiopia under its rule.
questions.explanation: In the late 13th century, the expanding kingdom of Damot was active in the region south of the Abay River, where it overran and dominated the kingdom of Bizamo before being pressured by the Oromo and Christian kingdom expansions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following major event marked the beginning of the "Dark age" in Europe?
options: The decline of the influence of the Catholic church
The decline of production to feed growing population
The collapse of the Western Roman Empire
The emergence of early capitalist relations
questions.explanation: Historically, the collapse of the Western Roman Empire in the 5th century marked the onset of the Early Middle Ages, frequently referred to in traditional historiography as the 'Dark Ages'.

questions.questionText: Why did the Reformation elites break away from the Catholic Church?
options: The conflict over power within the Church
The immorality of church leaders
The approval of new version of the Bible
The limited authority of the Pope
questions.explanation: The Protestant Reformation was largely sparked by widespread outrage over the corruption, financial abuses, and moral laxity among Catholic church leaders and the sale of indulgences.

questions.questionText: Why did the Portuguese and Ottoman Turkey involve in the 16th century conflict between the sultanate of Adal and Christian Kingdom?
options: To assert their sphere of influence in the Red Sea region.
Both wanted to get slaves in the interior parts of Ethiopia.
They sought to spread their respective religion in Ethiopia.
Both aspired to support their respective fellow believers in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: The intervention of Portugal and the Ottoman Empire in the 16th-century conflict was primarily driven by geopolitical competition and the desire to assert their strategic spheres of influence in the Red Sea and Indian Ocean trade routes.

questions.questionText: How did the expulsion of the Jesuits from Ethiopia in the 17th century influence subsequent Ethio-European relationship?
options: Ethiopia stopped ties until Europeans opened legations.
Almost all European governments mistrusted Ethiopia forever.
The Jesuits misinformed Europeans that Ethiopia was not good match.
The interaction between them interrupted for a century and half.
questions.explanation: Following the expulsion of the Jesuits by Emperor Fasilides, Ethiopia largely closed its doors to European missionaries and travelers, resulting in an interruption of direct interactions for about a century and a half.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Gondar city as an urban center?
options: The existence of diversified and large number of populations
The presence of separate living quarters for different religious groups
The limited interaction between the city and the rural society
The construction of magnificent castles and palaces
questions.explanation: Gondar maintained vibrant trade, economic, and social interactions with the surrounding rural society rather than having limited interaction.

questions.questionText: Why did the San people move to the Kalahari Desert in the mid-17th century? Due to the
options: pressure of the Dutch settlers.
changes of their livelihood to breeding.
depletion of resources.
conflicts with the neighboring San.
questions.explanation: The encroachment and pressure from Dutch settlers moving into the interior of South Africa pushed the indigenous San people further into arid regions like the Kalahari Desert.

questions.questionText: What was the effect of the Triangular Atlantic slave trade?
options: Strengthened Afro-American relations.
Depopulated Africa of its productive labor.
Restricted the industrialization of Europeans.
Brought the smallpox disease to America.
questions.explanation: The Transatlantic slave trade had devastating demographic consequences, severely depopulating regions of Africa of millions of its most productive young laborers.

questions.questionText: What was the basic factor for the consolidation of capitalism in modern Europe?
options: The expansion of the guild system
The shift from steam energy to water power
The emergence of the Bourgeoisies and proletariat classes
The shift from manual labor to machine production
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution and the fundamental shift from manual labor to machine production revolutionized manufacturing and solidified the capitalist economic system in modern Europe.

questions.questionText: What was the remarkable achievement of the French Revolution?
options: The abolishment of the monarchial system
The improvement in living conditions of the poor
The seizure of political power by the working class
The promulgation of a democratic constitution
questions.explanation: One of the most profound and immediate transformations of the French Revolution was the overthrow and abolishment of the absolute monarchical system in France.
